curated-gf-spirax-gf-alegreya-sc: Alegreya SC has a wide s that never tightens. Spirax up top is lopsided, with heavy stems making its hairlines look tiny, while the body's thick-thin shift stays faint and manageable over a good stretch of text.
curated-gf-splash-gf-ibm-plex-sans-thai-: Splash huddles its handwritten glyphs into a dense, closed-up scrawl. IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped is the opposite, with curves that refuse to close, and that open-versus-closed tension is the best thing about the pairing.
curated-gf-splash-gf-line-seed-jp: LINE Seed JP reads friendly and level, with horizontals as heavy as verticals. Over a longer stretch its counters keep letting the eye slip in and out, a sharp contrast to the closed, pen-drawn huddle of Splash.
curated-gf-square-peg-fs-recia: Recia reads sharp and a bit formal, its modulation visible mainly up close, and its openings stay generous at every weight. Square Peg, low and hand-drawn, makes a loose partner (say, for a hair accessories brand).
curated-gf-srisakdi-gf-belgrano: Blunt, clipped, almost carved. Srisakdi does hairline-free display work with little room between stems, while Belgrano is the one with open-mouthed curves that stay clear and a low, traditional feel.
curated-gf-srisakdi-gf-noto-sans-warang-: Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks rather than skylines, with wide channels leading into each counter. Srisakdi's clipped, hairline-free display letters sit moderate in height against that taller body, and that mismatch is the pairing's best quality.
curated-gf-stalemate-gf-electrolize: Lanky handwriting meets machined edges. Stalemate's capitals tower over its low lowercase, and Electrolize, with its open-jawed c like a pair of pliers, brings a modern, tidy counterweight that could suit children's museum signs.
curated-gf-stalinist-one-gf-noto-serif-b: Bold tall rounded lowercase and loose, rope-slack tracking mark Stalinist One as a loud, distinctive heading. Noto Serif Balinese settles in with a comfortable midpoint between flat and dramatic strokes, its lowercase standing tall enough to carry a longer passage.
curated-gf-stalinist-one-gf-noto-serif-o: Distinctive in every tall, rounded, loosely tracked letter, Stalinist One leads, with Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq following in a dignified, sizable lowercase (perhaps for a climbing gym). Shrink that heading, though, and its personality drains away.
curated-gf-stardos-stencil-gf-metrophobi: Stencil-bold stems sit beside fine scribed hairlines in Stardos Stencil, a loud heading that could front phone case art. Metrophobic follows with a smooth, unobstructed path around each bend, easy going on the eye.
